Section K is complete. Here's the TL;DR:
Edge GNN Paper vs. Asolaria's Graph:
Asolaria's "GNN" is not a GNN — it's a well-structured event graph with heuristic keyword-based risk scoring (edgeRiskEngine.js adds points for strings like "secret", "iam", "deploy"). The paper's three architectures (Prototype-GNN, Contrastive-GNN, GSL-GNN) represent a genuine leap — 91% → 96% accuracy with 1.5% false positive rate — by learning edge classifications instead of hand-coding them. However, Asolaria's existing infrastructure (rich edge semantics, actor→subject→target triples, freshness tracking, experimental edge prototypes) is excellent input scaffolding for bolting on a real GNN. The experimentalEdgePrototypes array is the right idea, just needs learned weights instead of hardcoded score functions.
The Tron World:
More of this exists than you might think. The Civilization World engine has 53 entities across 8 districts with motion states and route tracking. SwarmDesk integration has MQTT WSS transport ready, hook points documented in Dan's codebase, and live export payloads already flowing. What's missing is the actual 3D rendering on Dan's dashboard end and the GNN intelligence overlay.
Why Asolaria Forgets:
Three compounding failures: (1) Memory is a 300-turn sliding window — operational knowledge gets evicted, (2) no persistent task scheduler that executes jobs on a timetable, (3) all Google connectors are configured READ-ONLY so even if she remembered, she couldn't act. Fix #1 (persistent knowledge store) is the single highest priority — without it, everything else you build will also be forgotten.
Priority order: Persistent knowledge + scheduler → Google write scopes → SwarmDesk 3D rendering → GNN training pipeline → Prototype-GNN sidecar → Security gates → GSL-GNN → Full Tron world.


Section K: Edge GNN Paper Analysis, Tron World Vision, Google Ecosystem & Hybrid Control Architecture
K.1 — Edge-Level GNN Paper vs. Asolaria's Existing Graph System
K.1.1 — Paper Summary (Yaman, Siemens)
Three novel edge-level GNN architectures for network intrusion detection:
Prototype-GNN (94.24% accuracy): Distance-based classification using learnable class prototypes in embedding space. Edges are classified by proximity to prototype vectors rather than a linear head.
Contrastive-GNN (94.71%): Dual-loss architecture combining supervised contrastive learning with classification. Pulls same-class edge embeddings together, pushes different-class apart.
GSL-GNN (96.66%, 99.70% ROC-AUC, 1.5% FPR): Adaptive graph structure learning with dual-path GCN. Learns an optimal graph structure from data rather than using the given topology. This is the breakthrough contribution.
All three beat the EdgeLevelGCN baseline (91.87%) and outperform classical ML methods on NF-ToN-IoT-v2 dataset.
K.1.2 — What Asolaria Has Today
Asolaria's graph system is a runtime event journal + rule-based risk engine, not a GNN:
graphRuntimeStore.js: Append-only NDJSON event log. Each event has actor→subject→target triple, risk score, policy context. Schema version 1.0.
edgeRiskEngine.js: Deterministic heuristic scorer — keyword matching ("secret", "iam", "deploy" → +6; "provider", "phone" → +3), criticality bonuses, cross-domain penalties, approval state adjustments. Score maps to level (≥9=critical, ≥6=high, ≥3=medium, else low).
graphRuntimeQuery.js: Aggregation layer that builds node/edge graphs from raw events, computes freshness bands (hot/warm/cool/cold), suspicious edge ranking, graph diffs, activity timelines.
experimentalEdgePrototypes array (4 entries): Hand-coded scoring functions for provider-route, phone-loop, task-flow, privileged-control patterns. Each returns 0-1 similarity score. This is the closest thing to "classification" — but it's static pattern matching, not learned.
civilizationWorld.js: Entity registry mapping everything into 8 districts (Citadel, Colony, Perimeter, Gate Ring, Ledger Quarter, Workshop, Cloud Arc, World Bridge). Entities have motion states (moving/awake/disturbed/resting/steady).
K.1.3 — Gap Analysis: Paper vs. Reality
What Asolaria's graph system does well:
Rich edge semantics already captured: actor, subject, target with type/id/label/domain/criticality. This is better input data than raw network flows.
Temporal tracking (timestamps, freshness bands, activity timelines) provides the temporal features GNNs need.
The experimentalEdgePrototypes concept is correct in spirit — edge-level classification IS the right abstraction for this system.
Cross-domain detection (actorDomain ≠ targetDomain) maps directly to the paper's anomaly detection goal.
What's fundamentally missing:
No learned representations. The edge risk engine is 100% handcrafted rules. The paper's entire contribution is that learned embeddings outperform fixed rules. Asolaria can't adapt to novel attack patterns or operational anomalies.
No graph structure learning. GSL-GNN's key insight — learning the optimal graph topology from data — is completely absent. Asolaria treats the graph topology as given (actor→target connections from events).
No embedding space. There are no vector representations of nodes or edges. The experimentalEdgePrototypes score functions output a single float, not a learned embedding.
No contrastive learning. No mechanism to learn "what normal looks like" vs. "what anomalous looks like" from historical data.
No training pipeline. No dataset, no model, no inference. The NDJSON event log has the training data but no ML consumes it.
Verdict: Asolaria's GNN system is not a GNN. It's a well-structured event graph with heuristic risk scoring. The paper's architectures represent a genuine 3-5x improvement path in detection accuracy (91% → 96%) and dramatically lower false positive rates. However, the existing infrastructure (event schema, entity registry, district model, freshness tracking) is excellent input infrastructure for a real GNN.
K.1.4 — Recommended GNN Integration Path
Phase 1: Training data pipeline (prerequisite)
The NDJSON event log already captures labeled events. Add a groundTruth field to buildGraphEvent() for human-labeled events (normal/suspicious/malicious).
Export periodic graph snapshots in a format suitable for PyTorch Geometric or DGL.
Target: 10K+ labeled edge events before training.
Phase 2: Prototype-GNN implementation (lowest risk, fastest value)
Implement learnable prototypes for the 4 existing experimentalEdgePrototypes categories plus "benign."
Replace heuristic scoring with distance-to-prototype classification.
Can run as a sidecar Python service, called from scoreEdgeRisk() with fallback to heuristics.
Phase 3: GSL-GNN for topology learning (highest value, most complex)
Let the model learn which connections should exist vs. which are anomalous.
Critical for detecting novel cross-domain attacks that heuristic rules miss.
Requires the graph structure learning dual-path GCN architecture from the paper.
Phase 4: Real-time inference on MQTT graph events
Stream graph events through MQTT → GNN inference service → annotated risk scores back to MQTT.
SwarmDesk/Tron world visualizes the GNN's confidence and prototype distances in real time.

53 entities across 8 districts, 35 routes, 20 tracked events

Motion system: moving/awake/disturbed/resting/steady
Risk routes tracked: 0 critical, 0 high, 4 medium, 31 low
Colony projections: 8 online, 3 active agents
Task ledger: 571 total tasks, 69 open
SwarmDesk Integration (partially built):
swarmDeskExport.js builds live export payloads with graph, agent poll, trusted entities, world state
MQTT hybrid transport ready: wss://127.0.0.1:18885/mqtt (browser-safe WSS), raw broker mqtt://127.0.0.1:18883
MQTT topics: asolaria/test/local/world/state, agents/colony/status, runtime/health, graph/events

swarmdesk-browser-mqtt-hybrid.md documents exact hook points in swarmdesk-dashboard-hooks.js
swarmdesk-export-live.json and civilization-world-latest.json provide real snapshots

Already a trusted entity in the ecosystem
Has dashboard at /dashboard where the 3D visualization would live
API endpoints: /api/ai-provider-keys, /api/ai/chat-completion, /api/mcp
Existing code-city / network visualization from a "2000s programmer" perspective
K.2.2 — The Tron Architecture
The vision: Asolaria IS the MCP (Master Control Program) from Tron. Dan's Madness site provides the 3D "Grid" surface. Agents are visible programs with assigned tasks.
Layer 1: Backend (Asolaria Core)
The civilization world engine generates the entity/route/event data
MQTT publishes real-time state changes
Graph runtime tracks all edge events with risk scoring
This is the "truth layer" — everything visualized derives from here
Layer 2: Transport (MQTT + HTTP + MCP)
MQTT WSS for real-time streaming to browser (world state, colony status, graph events)
HTTP REST for export payloads, agent polling, task ledger queries
MCP (Omnispindle) for bidirectional tool invocation between Asolaria and SwarmDesk
Three redundant channels ensure the Tron world always has data even if one transport fails
Layer 3: Visual Surface (Dan's Madness Dashboard)
Consumes MQTT streams and renders 3D entity graph
Agents as visible moving entities in districts — hover shows tasks/plans on floating screens
Gates as checkpoints between districts with traffic flow visualization
Towers as sentinel watchers at the perimeter
Packets as visible data bundles being carried by towers
Routes as glowing pathways with color-coded risk levels
Security "inspection points" where Police agents (Sentinel, Watchdog) examine traffic
Layer 4: GNN Intelligence Overlay (new, from paper)
GNN-classified edges overlaid on the 3D visualization
Edges glow based on GNN confidence: green=benign, yellow=watch, red=suspicious
Prototype distances shown as proximity to archetype icons in the visual space
Arrested/quarantined agents shown in a containment zone when GNN flags anomalous behavior
K.2.3 — Three Hybrid Control Modes
Mode 1: Visual (Dan's Dashboard)
Human-in-the-loop via 3D world interaction
Click agents to see tasks, approve manifests, redirect work
Drag agents between districts to reassign
Visually identify bottlenecks and anomalies
Uses: Playwright-type automation for testing, browser-native for live ops
Mode 2: Backend (Asolaria API + CLI)
Direct REST API calls (/api/worker-runtime/*, /api/integrations/*)
Gemini CLI for headless autonomous operations
Codex/Claude terminals for complex multi-step orchestration
Scheduler/cron system for automated periodic tasks
Uses: Programmatic control, scheduled jobs, autonomous agent loops
Mode 3: MCP/Playwright Bridge
MCP tools invoked by external AI agents (Abacus, Cursor, etc.) to read/write Asolaria state
Playwright browser automation for testing the visual layer programmatically
Bridge between external AI services and internal state without giving them direct API access
Uses: External AI integration, automated QA, cross-platform coordination
K.3 — Google Ecosystem Connectivity & The Memory Problem
K.3.1 — Current Google Integration State
Connectors that exist:
googleConnector.js: OAuth2 flow for Gmail (readonly) + Calendar (readonly). Primary account hardcoded: plasmatoid@gmail.com. Scopes are READ-ONLY by default. Supports vault-stored or env-var credentials.
gcpConnector.js: GCP service account auth (JWT → access token). Default scope: cloud-platform.read-only. Allowed admin services list includes IAM, AI Platform, Discovery Engine, Generative Language, Speech, TTS, Drive, Docs, Gmail, Calendar. Service account key stored in encrypted vault.
geminiApiConnector.js: Gemini AI Studio API key auth. Default model: gemini-2.5-flash. Supports generation, multimodal, files API, embeddings.
geminiCliConnector.js: Spawns local Gemini CLI process. Auth via GEMINI_API_KEY or GOOGLE_API_KEY env vars. Supports approval modes (default/auto_edit/yolo/plan).
geminiLiveConnector.js: (not read, but exists) Likely WebSocket-based live Gemini interaction.
vertexConnector.js: (not read, but exists) Vertex AI integration for heavy compute.
What the owner wants Gemini/Google to do:
Manage and control ALL Google Cloud APIs
Manage ALL Google services (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, YouTube, etc.)
Publish the Asolaria app
Connect to YouTube, LinkedIn, all Google services
Operate on both computer AND cell phone
Act as SUPER ADMIN across jbrowndevelopment and plasmatoid@gmail.com subscriptions
What's actually configured:
OAuth scopes are READ-ONLY (gmail.readonly, calendar.readonly)
GCP default scope is READ-ONLY (cloud-platform.read-only)
No write scopes configured for Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, YouTube, or any other service
No YouTube API integration exists
No LinkedIn API integration exists (credential stored in vault but no connector)
No app publishing pipeline exists
Phone integration exists but is a separate connector chain, not Google-unified
K.3.2 — Why Asolaria "Doesn't Remember" / Can't Act on Schedule
This is the critical diagnosis. Three compounding failures:
1. Memory system is a sliding window, not persistent knowledge:
memoryStore.js: 300-turn rolling window (maxTurns = 300)
Snapshots every 5 minutes, keeps last 24 snapshots
No WAL (Write-Ahead Log) — crash during write = data loss
writeJsonAtomic() uses tmp file + rename (good), but the in-memory cache cache = null resets on restart
Memory is conversation-scoped (turn-based chat history), NOT a knowledge base or task scheduler
When memory fills, oldest turns are silently dropped (.slice(-maxTurns))
Compaction strips "boilerplate" turns but no semantic prioritization of what's important
Result: Google API management tasks, scheduled actions, and long-term operational knowledge get evicted from memory as new conversations push them out. Asolaria literally forgets.
2. No persistent task scheduler with execution guarantees:
Cron/scheduler references exist in server.js but they're interval-based observers (model-audit, external-observed-prune), not a task execution engine
There's no durable job queue that says "at 9am, check Google API quotas" or "every Monday, verify OAuth tokens"
The task ledger tracks 571 tasks but they're passive records — no daemon wakes up and executes them
OpenClaw cron exists but appears to be for external scheduled operations, not Google management
Result: Even if Asolaria "knows" it should manage Google APIs, there's no persistent mechanism to trigger that action on schedule.
3. Google connectors are configured for read-only passive observation, not active management:
OAuth scopes deliberately restricted to readonly
GCP scope is cloud-platform.read-only
No service-to-service automation for Google Workspace admin
No Google Admin SDK integration (needed for enterprise management)
No programmatic deployment pipeline for app publishing
Result: Even if memory and scheduling worked perfectly, the connectors can't write/manage/deploy — they can only read.
K.3.3 — What Needs to Change
Memory → Persistent Knowledge Store:
Separate operational knowledge ("plasmatoid@gmail.com OAuth needs refresh") from conversation history
Implement a durable key-value or document store for standing orders, API states, credential health
Add a "standing directives" layer that survives memory compaction
Scheduling → Durable Task Executor:
Implement a persistent job queue (could be as simple as a cron-definition file + a daemon loop)
Jobs: OAuth token refresh, API health checks, quota monitoring, security audit, app deployment checks
Each job linked to a specific connector and recorded in the graph event log
Google Scopes → Write Access:
Expand OAuth scopes to include write access for services Asolaria needs to manage
Add Google Admin SDK for Workspace management
Add YouTube Data API for channel management
Add Play Developer API for app publishing
Each scope expansion goes through the approval-path edge type in the graph system
